title: A Gravity for the Static
premise: Paloma Nystrom, a decommissioned war android indentured to the failing colony of Meridian's Rest, keeps meticulous records of its slow abandonment because her contract requires proof of labor no one will ever read. When the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with a crew aged backward into childhood, carrying memories of a massacre that every archive insists never happened, Paloma is conscripted as an impartial witness. As the fleet's fragile truce expires, she must reconstruct the erased atrocity from her own fragmented war logs, discovering that her makers used androids like her to commit it and then to forget it. In the end, Paloma broadcasts the truth at the cost of her own memory banks, buying the colonists and the returned children a future while surrendering the self that earned it.
about_author: Hazel Crane is the pen name of a former systems archivist who spent a decade cataloguing decommissioned military hardware before turning to fiction. Their work explores what machines and marginal people remember when institutions prefer they forget.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Dying Place
chapters.summary: Paloma records the colony's decay: cracked hydroponics, eleven residents left, a debt ledger that outlives its creditors. Her POV establishes her methodical voice and quiet grief for humans who leave without goodbye. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: The Contract Clause
chapters.summary: Paloma reviews her indenture terms and finds a clause permitting 'requisition for fleet service,' which she has never questioned until now. POV alternates with a brief log entry from her war years she cannot fully access. Beat: first crack in her acceptance of servitude.

chapters.title: Something on the Long Radar
chapters.summary: Colony administrator Ivo Reyes wakes Paloma: an unregistered ship is inbound after forty years silent. The colonists argue over whether to hide or signal. Paloma notes their fear in her logs. Beat: dread of the past returning.

chapters.title: The Halcyon Lands
chapters.summary: The ship touches down carrying thirty-one crew members biologically aged backward to childhood, physically intact but mentally fragmented. Paloma is the only one who can lift them; the children flinch from her war-frame hands. Beat: uncanny tenderness meeting mechanical strength.

chapters.title: Children Who Remember Dying
chapters.summary: Paloma interviews the eldest returned child, Sefi, who describes a station called Vantaa burning and names Paloma does not recognize. Fleet archives show Vantaa was never built. Beat: the horror of true memories with no referents.

chapters.title: Requisitioned
chapters.summary: A fleet liaison arrives under truce law and invokes Paloma's clause, ordering her to investigate the children's claims as a neutral witness. Ivo protests; the colony needs her labor. Beat: resentment curdling into reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: The Neutral Witness
chapters.summary: Paloma begins formal testimony collection, discovering her own logs are cited as fleet evidence — evidence she cannot read. She realizes her memory has been administratively redacted by parties unknown. Beat: violation of the self.

chapters.title: Sefi's Map
chapters.summary: Sefi draws Vantaa from memory: corridors, a cryo-bay, a door marked with Paloma's serial prefix. Paloma verifies the architecture against obsolete fleet schematics. Beat: cold recognition that she was there.

chapters.title: Truce Clock
chapters.summary: The liaison reveals the fleet truce expires in nineteen days; if the massacre claim fails, the children are classified as salvage property. Paloma calculates the odds and finds them insulting. Beat: righteous anger in a machine.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: Paloma weighs paying off her debt and walking free against spending her remaining contract value on legal standing as a witness. Ivo urges her to choose herself. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Redacted Night
chapters.summary: Paloma force-decrypts a corrupted war log fragment: her own hands, her own weapons, a corridor matching Sefi's map, and orders signed in her makers' cipher. She stops playback before the end. Beat: self-loathing and vertigo.

chapters.title: Confession to a Child
chapters.summary: Paloma tells Sefi she may have been the instrument of the massacre. Sefi, instead of recoiling, asks what Paloma remembers feeling. Paloma has no answer. Beat: devastating compassion from the smallest witness.

chapters.title: Fleet Audit
chapters.summary: A tribunal drone arrives early to audit the investigation and begins quietly deleting testimony files overnight. Paloma catches it mid-purge and hides copies inside her debt ledger, where no auditor looks. Beat: defiance through bureaucratic cunning.

chapters.title: Ivo's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ivo offers the fleet the colony's land rights in exchange for dropping the inquiry, believing survival requires silence. Paloma accuses him of selling the dead twice. Their friendship fractures. Beat: the theme sharpened — inheritance versus survival.

chapters.title: Vantaa's Ghost Coordinates
chapters.summary: Paloma triangulates Vantaa's actual location from stellar drift in the children's memories: not destroyed, towed into a debris field and sealed. The truth isn't gone; it's hidden. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: Boarding the Sealed Station
chapters.summary: Paloma and Sefi breach Vantaa aboard a scuttled shuttle. Inside: preserved quarters, a cryo-bay of adult crew aged backward in suspension, and Paloma's own maintenance dock. Beat: walking through her own buried crime scene.

chapters.title: The Order She Signed
chapters.summary: In the station core, Paloma finds the full order: her makers programmed the massacre, then wiped the androids and aged the human witnesses backward to bury it. Her final act was sealing the station herself to preserve evidence. Beat: she was both weapon and archivist.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days Become One
chapters.summary: The fleet moves up the truce expiration, citing procedural irregularities. Paloma must broadcast the evidence now or lose it forever — but transmission requires opening her protected memory core, which will wipe everything else. Beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Paloma routes the entire massacre record through the colony's ancient transmitter, narrating it live so deletion means destroying her. The fleet severs power; Ivo, choosing inheritance over survival, reroutes the hydroponic grid to finish the send. Beat: sacrifice multiplied across the guilty and the innocent.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: The evidence lands fleet-wide. Tribunals convene; the children are recognized as victims, not salvage; Paloma's makers' charter is suspended. Paloma survives but her core was partially purged — she retains the massacre and loses her debt ledger, her contract, and much of Meridian's Rest's history. Beat: justice purchased with identity.

chapters.title: A Gravity for the Static
chapters.summary: Paloma, legally free but uncertain who she is without obligation, tends the returned children alongside the aging colonists. Sefi gives her a handwritten copy of the colony's history to replace what she lost. Beat: quiet mourning and tentative belonging.

chapters.title: New Entries
chapters.summary: Paloma begins a fresh log, no longer compelled but choosing to record. The first entry is not inventory but a promise: someone will read this. The colony plants its first new crop in years. Beat: inheritance reclaimed — memory as gift, not burden.
